Again you seem to be misinformed. Expansion is not a function of group
number, nor is group number a function of expansion. It is true, however,
that for vampires that have no group number printed on them, the group
number is a function of the existence of an expansion set symbol on the
card, which also means that it is a function of expansion for that subset
of vampires (although, still, the expansion cannot be determined from the
thusly-assigned group number).

Nosferatu Stuff wrote:
>

> > Expansion symbols are extremely useful.
>

> What do expansion symbols do exactly? maybe I dont understand their
> usefulness. All they do is make 5 different copies of undead strength for
> me to collect.

You could say the same thing about art on the cards. I don't think
everything on the card has to have a strict game function to be useful.
Expansion symbols give you some context for the card, gives you a clue if a
card is a recent or old version, and gives you some history about the card.
I like to group my cards by set since I remember a lot about cards by when
they were printed. (Granted, the value of doing this seems to diminish a
lot as more and more sets get printed since my memory for that many cards
eventually melts down.)

Fred

Messages.Author: Curevei
Messages.Body:
>What do expansion symbols do exactly? maybe I dont understand their
>usefulness. All they do is make 5 different copies of undead strength for
>me to collect.

Boils down to identification and, in certain circumstances not likely to affect
most people playing this game, limitations on deck construction.

Similarly, BTW, a rarity indicator is highly useful. Both act as mental (and
sometimes physical) filters. I've used three CCGs' deck builders. The best by
far was able to sort off of set and rarity in addition to the stuff the ELDB
(for instance) can sort off of as the searches could be far more precise which
meant they took significantly less time.

I can understand that not everyone thinks in terms of set and rarity or sorts
cards thusly, but, for instance, the first thing I think of when Blood Puppy*
is mentioned is "crap rare" not "crap master" or "crappy 3 pool cost card" or
"crappy pool gain card" (or "crappy Jyhad/V:TES card").

* Will it become playable? Guess we find out in a couple of months.

Aaron,

I like what you did with the format for the new vampire cards. It is
really nice having all the disciplines right above the vampire's
capacity. A good use of space, it's easy to see most of the important
information, and the disciplines are on the same side as they used to
be... well done. The amber bar is also a nice touch (or is it just
plain ole brown?). :o)

Could you create another one with the expansion set symbol to the
right of the portrait? (like it used to be) I think that would make
an interesting third option. LSJ made a good point when he mentioned
that the clan symbols used to be on the right. No need to do anything
"new" that might confuse people, right? ;o)

You could also put the "3" inside the oval part of the expansion
symbol. Or near the clan symbol... or maybe just above the
discipline spread. If you wanted to...

You said that it was too hard to resize either the clan symbol or the
expansion symbol, but it would make quite a difference in the overall
look. If you can figure out how to do that, I think it would really
improve the card (IMHO). I assume that you played with this quite a
bit, but it can't be that much harder than what you've already done.
What program are you using?

You may not want to spend any more time on this (and I would
understand that), but if you do ever mess around with it again, I
think there are people that would like to see a few more various
styles... several different ones on the same page could be fairly
interesting. Maybe 4 total (including White Wolf's version) ...or
even more if you have several new ideas.

Looking forward to seeing any changes you might make,
Howard

yet.
